tools.name: spaces
tools.description: List the spaces (name and id). Run this first when no space id is known — find, describe and create take a space id from here.
tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws (p-limit)? ws "}"
p-limit ::= "\"limit\"" ws ":" ws number ws
ws ::= [ \t\n]*
string ::= "\"" schar* "\""
schar ::= [^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt] | "u" hex hex hex hex)
hex ::= [0-9a-fA-F]
number ::= "-"? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]+)?
boolean ::= "true" | "false"
scalar ::= string | number | boolean | "null"
scalarlist ::= "[" ws (scalar (ws "," ws scalar)*)? ws "]"
flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist
flatobject ::= "{" ws (string ws ":" ws flatvalue (ws "," ws string ws ":" ws flatvalue)*)? ws "}"

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search objects in a space by query, type or filter. Returns numbered handles (1, 2, …) the other tools accept as `object`. Each find renumbers the handles. Given none of the three it matches nothing and lists the space instead — unnumbered, and not addressable.

filter.description: compact filter string, e.g. Done = false AND Due_date < currentWeek() — string values in double quotes; write multi-word property names with underscores (Due_date); a name no identifier can spell (C++, 50% done) cannot be filtered here

tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws p-space ("," ws p-query)? ("," ws p-type)? ("," ws p-filter)? ("," ws p-limit)? ws "}"
p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-query ::= "\"query\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-type ::= "\"type\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-filter ::= "\"filter\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-limit ::= "\"limit\"" ws ":" ws number ws
ws ::= [ \t\n]*
string ::= "\"" schar* "\""
schar ::= [^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt] | "u" hex hex hex hex)
hex ::= [0-9a-fA-F]
number ::= "-"? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]+)?
boolean ::= "true" | "false"
scalar ::= string | number | boolean | "null"
scalarlist ::= "[" ws (scalar (ws "," ws scalar)*)? ws "]"
flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist
flatobject ::= "{" ws (string ws ":" ws flatvalue (ws "," ws string ws ":" ws flatvalue)*)? ws "}"

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read an object. mode=full (the default) returns every block with its TEXT and the short label the editing tools take as `block` — this is the read an edit needs. mode=outline returns the same blocks with text truncated to 80 runes — a cheaper survey; copy exact text from mode=full. Reading a Query or Collection returns its definition (source type, filter, sort) and numbers its rows like find does, so they can be passed as `object`.

mode.description: default full; outline truncates each block's text to 80 runes

object.description: the object: a handle number from the last find (1, 2, …) or a full object id

space.description: the space the object is in — optional: needed only when no find has run yet, and ignored for a handle number, which the last find already places

tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws p-object ("," ws p-space)? ("," ws p-mode)? ws "}"
p-object ::= "\"object\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-mode ::= "\"mode\"" ws ":" ws e-mode ws
e-mode ::= "\"full\"" | "\"outline\""
ws ::= [ \t\n]*
string ::= "\"" schar* "\""
schar ::= [^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt] | "u" hex hex hex hex)
hex ::= [0-9a-fA-F]
number ::= "-"? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]+)?
boolean ::= "true" | "false"
scalar ::= string | number | boolean | "null"
scalarlist ::= "[" ws (scalar (ws "," ws scalar)*)? ws "]"
flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist
flatobject ::= "{" ws (string ws ":" ws flatvalue (ws "," ws string ws ":" ws flatvalue)*)? ws "}"

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Describe a type before creating or editing objects of it: its property names, formats, and live select option names. Call this first — property names and option names must match exactly. When a property shows more options than fit, ask again with options set to that property name.

options.description: list ONE property's select options in full instead of describing the type, e.g. Status

starting_with.description: with options: only options starting with this text

tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws p-space "," ws p-type ("," ws p-options)? ("," ws p-starting-with)? ws "}"
p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-type ::= "\"type\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-options ::= "\"options\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-starting-with ::= "\"starting_with\"" ws ":" ws string ws

flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist

tools.name: create
tools.description: Create an object. properties uses the type's property names (describe first); markdown becomes the body. Date values accept today, tomorrow, +Nd, weekday names; @me means the calling user; object properties (assignee, related objects) accept a handle number from the last find or the object's exact name.

markdown.description: markdown body: headings, lists, - [ ] checkboxes, ``` fences, quotes, tables

properties.description: property name → value; select values are option NAMES

tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws p-space "," ws p-type "," ws p-name ("," ws p-properties)? ("," ws p-markdown)? ws "}"
p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-type ::= "\"type\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-name ::= "\"name\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-properties ::= "\"properties\"" ws ":" ws flatobject ws
p-markdown ::= "\"markdown\"" ws ":" ws string ws

flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist

tools.name: set_properties
tools.description: Change property values on an object — or on several at once, passed as a comma-separated list. set replaces a value; add/remove edit list values (tags, assignees) without rewriting the whole list. Option names must exist (describe shows them). Values of object properties (assignee, related objects) take a handle number or the object's exact name as well as an id. type changes the object's type (a page to a Task, a note to a page); only same-family layouts convert, and a refused conversion names the types the object can take.

add.description: list property name → entries to append

object.description: the object: a handle number from the last find (1, 2, …) or a full object id; several objects separate with commas ("1,2,3") — the same change is written to each, one at a time

remove.description: list property name → entries to delete

space.description: the space the object is in — optional: needed only when no find has run yet, and ignored for a handle number, which the last find already places

type.description: a type name the object becomes, e.g. Task; applied before set/add/remove in the same edit

p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-set ::= "\"set\"" ws ":" ws flatobject ws

tools.name: add_blocks
tools.description: Add content to an object, written as markdown (headings, lists, - [ ] checkboxes, ``` fences, quotes, tables). Omit after/under to append at the end of the document.

after.description: insert after this block (a block label from read (5 chars) or a full block id)

object.description: the object: a handle number from the last find (1, 2, …) or a full object id

space.description: the space the object is in — optional: needed only when no find has run yet, and ignored for a handle number, which the last find already places

under.description: insert as last child of this block

tools.gbnf:
root ::= "{" ws p-object "," ws p-markdown ("," ws p-space)? ("," ws p-after)? ("," ws p-under)? ws "}"
p-object ::= "\"object\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-space ::= "\"space\"" ws ":" ws string ws
p-markdown ::= "\"markdown\"" ws ":" ws string ws

flatvalue ::= scalar | scalarlist
flatobject ::= "{" ws (string ws ":" ws flatvalue (ws "," ws string ws ":" ws flatvalue)*)? ws "}"

tools.name: edit_text
tools.description: Replace text inside one block: give a short exact snippet to find and its replacement. The snippet must occur exactly once in the block. block is optional — when omitted, the snippet itself must pin down exactly one block. Text is markdown source — ** [ ] etc. format.

block.description: a block label from read (5 chars) or a full block id; optional — when omitted the find snippet locates the block, and must match exactly one

find.description: exact text to replace, as it appears in the block

object.description: the object: a handle number from the last find (1, 2, …) or a full object id

replace.description: the new text — empty deletes the found text

space.description: the space the object is in — optional: needed only when no find has run yet, and ignored for a handle number, which the last find already places

filterGrammar.gbnf:
root ::= fws orexpr fws
orexpr ::= andexpr (rws "OR" rws andexpr)*
andexpr ::= primary (rws "AND" rws primary)*
primary ::= "(" fws orexpr fws ")" | leaf
leaf ::= key fws symcond | key rws wordcond
symcond ::= compare fws value
          | eqop fws valuelist
wordcond ::= ("NOT" rws)? "CONTAINS" rws value
           | ("NOT" rws)? "IN" fws valuelist
           | ("NOT" rws)? "HAS" rws "ALL" fws valuelist
           | "IS" rws ("NOT" rws)? "EMPTY"
           | "EXISTS"
compare ::= ">=" | "<=" | "!=" | "=" | ">" | "<"
eqop ::= "=" | "!="
valuelist ::= "(" fws fvalue (fws "," fws fvalue)* fws ")"
value ::= fvalue
fvalue ::= fstring | fnumber | "true" | "false" | preset
preset ::= presetname fws "(" fws ")" | countname fws "(" fws fnumber fws ")"
presetname ::= "yesterday" | "today" | "tomorrow" | "lastWeek" | "currentWeek" | "nextWeek" | "lastMonth" | "currentMonth" | "nextMonth" | "lastYear" | "currentYear" | "nextYear"
countname ::= "daysAgo" | "daysFromNow"
key ::= [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]*
fstring ::= "\"" fchar* "\""
fchar ::= [^"\\] | "\\" ["\\nt]
fnumber ::= "-"? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]*)?
fws ::= [ \t]*
rws ::= [ \t]+
examples: done = false AND (due_date < currentWeek() OR due_date IS EMPTY)
tags HAS ALL ("urgent", "q3") AND assignee IS NOT EMPTY
